method: re-parse every .py in the corpus E391 walks, import E638's two-depth site grouping and E640's owner split, keep the sites that have no enclosing function and carry a store/delete, and for each publish the module-level guard region it executes in (bare body / main guard / other conditional / loop / with / try / try-else / except handler / finally), the full nesting chain, the bucket E643 assigned, and whether any write member's literal key names one of the counted row keys E633's read lines use
population_source: 13110 Python files of the tree corpus; the population is every two-depth write site E640's owner split leaves without a function

bare_module_body.source: st["r1334"]["s7_correction"] = ["earlier text claimed nothing was re-registered: " + old]

limits: 'guard' is the innermost module-level region holding the site's (line, column) and the chain is published beside it, so a site inside a for-loop inside an if is conditional>loop rather than a single label
guard_depth counts guard regions, not AST block nodes: try's else and finally carry no node of their own, so this depth is one larger than E643's module_block_depth exactly on those two regions
a main guard is only ``__name__ == '__main__'`` (either operand order); ``__name__ != '__main__'`` is published as an ordinary conditional because its body is the half that runs at import

the execution lines (import_time) are read off the guard kind alone; a loop body may run zero times, a with body may raise inside the context manager, and a conditional may be false -- those are named as such rather than resolved by evaluating the test
a write site outside the module body (a class body, a lambda, a comprehension) is published with guard outside_module_body and is never counted as a bare module body site
only literal keys can name a counted key; a computed subscript keeps the row but can never match, so the key column is a lower bound on what the site could address
an augmented assignment (``P['k'] += 1``) is an ast store, so it counts as a write here exactly as it does in E640

the exclusion list drops only this study's own files, so the E6xx study scripts stay inside the population and the residual is slightly larger than E643's published 2,641; the difference is published as delta_vs_source_face with its reason
files over 1MB are skipped rather than parsed (E391's cap) and are counted apart
